231	    """The write target relative to the project root, normalised — or None when it will not resolve.

233	    None fails OPEN (see the module docstring): an unresolvable path is not classified as product

238	        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.abspath(absolute), os.path.abspath(cwd))

265	def _verb(tokens):
266	    """The command verb: the first token that is a command NAME rather than shell syntax.
267	
268	    Skipped on the way: `VAR=value` assignments (structural, not listed), the POSIX reserved words
269	    that open a compound command, and the small wrapper set. A leading `(` or `{` is stripped off
270	    the token itself, because `(python x)` writes the subshell's opening bracket against the name.
271	    """
272	    for token in tokens:
273	        bare = token.strip("\"'").lstrip("({")
274	        if not bare:
275	            continue  # a bare bracket: syntax, not a name
276	        if "=" in bare and not bare.startswith("-"):
277	            continue  # VAR=value prefix
278	        low = os.path.basename(bare).lower()
279	        if low in _WRAPPERS or low in _RESERVED_WORDS:
280	            continue
281	        return low
282	    return ""

284	
285	def _blank_quoted(text):
286	    """`text` with the CONTENT of quoted spans blanked out, plus whether every quote was closed.
287	
288	    Length-preserving on purpose: an offset in the result is the same offset in the original, so
289	    every reader below can ask "is this character quoted?" without a second pass. Both callers need
290	    that — the separator scan (a `;` inside quotes is data, not a separator) and the here-document
291	    scan (a `<<` inside quotes opens no body).
292	
293	    The second return value is the honest part: when a quote never closes, this reading is not
294	    trustworthy, and the callers fall back to the quote-BLIND text.
295	
296	    THE DIRECTION OF THAT FALLBACK IS NOT THE SAME FOR BOTH CALLERS, and pretending it was is what
297	    round 3 caught. For the separator scan it means MORE splitting, so more is judged. For the
298	    here-document scan it means a quoted `<<EOF` becomes visible and opens a body that is not one —
299	    which would have made the rest of the command disappear. What holds that direction is not this
300	    function but `_without_heredoc_bodies`, which drops a body only once its terminator has been
301	    SEEN; with the fallback the terminator is not there, so nothing is dropped.
302	    """
303	    out, quote = [], ""
304	    for char in text:
305	        if quote:
306	            out.append(char if char == quote else " ")
307	            if char == quote:
308	                quote = ""
309	        else:
310	            if char in "'\"":
311	                quote = char
312	            out.append(char)
313	    return "".join(out), not quote

316	def _heredoc_delimiter(line):
317	    """The delimiter word of the here-document this line opens, or None.
318	
319	    Read off the line's QUOTE MASK with comments cut away, so a `<<` that is quoted data or sits in
320	    a comment opens nothing. The delimiter word itself is then read from the line as written; the
321	    quotes around it are stripped because they decide EXPANSION inside the body, and this reader
322	    never expands anything.
323	    """
324	    mask = _quote_mask(line)
325	    comment = _COMMENT.search(mask)
326	    if comment:
327	        mask = mask[:comment.start()]
328	    found = _HEREDOC_START.search(mask)
329	    if not found:
330	        return None
331	    word = _HEREDOC_WORD.match(line[found.end():])
332	    if not word:
333	        return None
334	    return next((group for group in word.groups() if group is not None), None)
335	
336	
337	def _without_heredoc_bodies(command):
338	    """`command` with the BODY of every TERMINATED here-document removed — it is data, not commands.
339	
340	    A body line is not executed by the shell, so judging it is an over-refusal: it hit the ALLOWED
341	    plan-artefact path (`cat > project_memory/product/masterplan.md <<'EOF' ...`), measured in the
342	    TSK-0032 rework. The redirection LINE itself stays and is still judged.
343	
344	    THE TERMINATOR IS REQUIRED, and that is the whole safety of this function (TSK-0032 round 3 N1).
345	    A body is only dropped once its delimiter line has actually been SEEN; when the input ends
346	    first, every buffered line is given back and judged. Otherwise anything that merely looked like
347	    a `<<` swallowed the entire rest of the command — three measured spellings, one of which was a
348	    QUOTED `<<EOF` made visible again by the unbalanced-quote fallback. The price is an
349	    over-refusal, and it is the direction this hook wants: a here-document whose terminator is not
350	    in the same tool call has its body judged as commands.
351	
352	    THE BODY IS READ LINE BY LINE, never joined across a continuation — measured against a real
353	    bash (round 3): inside a `<<'EOF'` body a trailing backslash is literal and the next `EOF`
354	    closes the document (the command after it RUNS, so it must be judged: that was N2), while
355	    inside a `<<EOF` body the shell joins and swallows further. Stopping at the first delimiter
356	    line is therefore never earlier than the shell stops and never later — this reader can only
357	    judge MORE than the shell executes, which is the safe direction and the over-refusal named in
358	    POST_V2_WISHLIST L39.
359	    """
360	    lines = command.split("\n")
361	    kept, index = [], 0
362	    while index < len(lines):
363	        line = lines[index]
364	        kept.append(line)
365	        index += 1
366	        delimiter = _heredoc_delimiter(line)
367	        if delimiter is None:
368	            continue
369	        body = []
370	        while index < len(lines):
371	            candidate = lines[index]
372	            body.append(candidate)
373	            index += 1
374	            if candidate.strip() == delimiter:
375	                # terminator seen: the buffered body was data after all. Replace it with BLANK
376	                # lines, not nothing — the line COUNT has to survive, or a later continuation join
377	                # would bridge the cut this made and glue a real command onto the `cat` segment
378	                # (round 4 R3-1: the redirection line itself ended on a `\`). Blanks name no engine.
379	                body = [""] * len(body)
380	                break
381	        kept.extend(body)  # blanks when terminated, the whole buffer when the input ran out
382	    return "\n".join(kept)
383

385	def _quote_mask(text):
386	    """`text` with quoted content blanked when the quoting is readable, and `text` itself when not."""
387	    blanked, balanced = _blank_quoted(text)
388	    return blanked if balanced else text
389

391	def _segments(command):
392	    """The command's top-level segments: the spans between UNQUOTED separator characters.
393	
394	    Two adjacent separators (`&&`, `||`, `|&`) simply yield an empty span between them, which names
395	    no engine — so the separator set needs single characters only.
396	    """
397	    mask = _quote_mask(command)
398	    found, start = [], 0
399	    for index, char in enumerate(mask):
400	        if char in _SEPARATORS:
401	            found.append(command[start:index])
402	            start = index + 1
403	    found.append(command[start:])
404	    return found
405	
406	
407	def _tokens(segment):
408	    """Split a segment at UNQUOTED whitespace, keeping a quoted span whole.
409	
410	    A quoted argument is one word to the shell, so `"a (b) c"` is a single token that ends in `"`,
411	    not in `)`, and a `--help` inside it is not a flag of its own (TSK-0032 round 4 R3-2/R3-3 —
412	    both were the mask going unconsulted at tokenisation). When the quoting does not close,
413	    tokenising cannot be trusted, so it falls back to a naive split, which judges MORE.
414	    """
415	    if not _blank_quoted(segment)[1]:
416	        return segment.split()
417	    tokens, current, quote = [], [], ""
418	    for char in segment:
419	        if quote:
420	            current.append(char)
421	            if char == quote:
422	                quote = ""
423	        elif char in "'\"":
424	            quote = char
425	            current.append(char)
426	        elif char.isspace():
427	            if current:
428	                tokens.append("".join(current))
429	                current = []
430	        else:
431	            current.append(char)
432	    if current:
433	        tokens.append("".join(current))
434	    return tokens
435	
436	
437	def _name_positions(tokens):
438	    """Every index in a segment where a command NAME can begin.
439	
440	    The beginning, and whatever follows a token that CLOSES a header rather than being a command:
441	    a `case` pattern (`a)`) and a function definition (`f()`) both put a word ending in `)` where a
442	    command name would otherwise stand, and the command comes after it (TSK-0032 round 3 N3). The
443	    tokens are quote-respecting (`_tokens`), so a `)` in the prose of a quoted argument ends its
444	    token in a quote, not in `)`, and opens no position (round 4 R3-2).
445	    """
446	    yield 0
447	    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
448	        if token.endswith(")") and index + 1 < len(tokens):
449	            yield index + 1
450	
451	
452	def _reads_the_engine(tokens):
453	    """True when this invocation only READS the engine instead of driving it.
454	
455	    A help FLAG counts wherever it stands (measured: argparse prints help and exits 0 even after a
456	    subcommand). A read SUBCOMMAND counts only in SUBCOMMAND POSITION — the first word after the
457	    engine path that is neither an option nor the value of the option before it. That is what the
458	    shipped read forms look like (`harness.py doctor`, `kernel.cli --root project_memory doctor`),
459	    and it is what `capture doctor` is not.
460	
461	    The tokens are quote-respecting (`_tokens`), so a help flag inside a quoted VALUE
462	    (`--body "see --help for details"`) is one token with the quotes still on it and is not read as
463	    a flag — argparse would not either (round 4 R3-3).
464	    """
465	    bare = [token.strip("\"'") for token in tokens]
466	    if any(token in _HELP_FLAGS for token in bare):
467	        return True
468	    engine = next((index for index, token in enumerate(bare)
469	                   if token.endswith("harness.py") or token == "kernel.cli"), None)
470	    if engine is None:
471	        return False
472	    after_option = False
473	    for token in bare[engine + 1:]:
474	        if token.startswith("-"):
475	            after_option = "=" not in token  # `--root x` carries its value in the next word
476	            continue
477	        if after_option:
478	            after_option = False
479	            continue
480	        return token in _READ_SUBCOMMANDS
481	    return False

483	
484	def _segment_drives_engine(segment):
485	    """True when this single command segment RUNS the work engine (not just names or reads it)."""
486	    if "harness.py" not in segment and "kernel.cli" not in segment:
487	        return False  # does not name the work engine
488	    tokens = _tokens(segment)
489	    for start in _name_positions(tokens):
490	        rest = tokens[start:]
491	        verb = _verb(rest)
492	        # names the engine but does not RUN it (e.g. `cat scripts/harness.py`, `grep x harness.py`):
493	        # reading is never derivation. Only a python interpreter or the script itself in verb
494	        # position drives it.
495	        if not (verb.startswith("python") or verb in ("py", "pythonw", "harness.py")):
496	            continue
497	        if _reads_the_engine(rest):
498	            continue  # doctor / --help: a read of the engine, not derivation

503	def _segment_touches_the_marker(segment):
504	    """True when this segment names the guard's own marker with anything but a known READ verb.
505	
506	    The allowlist runs the other way round from every other set in this file, and that is the point:
507	    an unlisted verb is refused, so the cost of a reader nobody listed is friction, while the cost
508	    of a remover nobody listed would be the guard switching itself off.
509	    """
510	    if _MARKER_WORD not in segment:
511	        return False
512	    for start in _name_positions(segment.split()):
513	        if _verb(segment.split()[start:]) not in _READ_VERBS:
514	            return True
515	    return False
516	
517	
518	def _handle_ask(tool_input):
519	    """Refuse only the AskUserQuestion that INITIATES the scope-approval flow (marker present).
520	
521	    NARROW: keyed on the approval-request marker, so normal asking/answering/plan-refinement — the
522	    whole point of the soft variant — stays allowed. The residue is named in the module docstring: a
523	    hallucinated approval question that OMITS the marker cannot be told apart from an ordinary one.
524	    Fail-open: a payload that will not serialise is not classified.
525	    """
526	    try:
527	        blob = json.dumps(tool_input, default=str)
528	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
529	        return  # unserialisable: not judged (fail-open, module docstring)
530	    if _APR_REQUEST_MARKER.search(blob):
531	        _refuse_approval_request()
532	
533	
534	def _handle_shell(tool_input):
535	    raw = str(tool_input.get("command") or "")
536	    if not raw.strip():
537	        _allow()
538	    # ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Here-document bodies are cut out FIRST, on the raw text, because that
539	    # is where a delimiter is still readable as quoted or unquoted and the shell's own joining rule
540	    # depends on it (round 3 N2). Only then are continuations joined, and only then does `_norm`
541	    # run — it turns every backslash into `/`, which would hide both (rework F1).
542	    command = _norm(_CONTINUATION.sub(" ", _without_heredoc_bodies(raw)))
543	    # Judge EACH segment on its own (TSK-0031): a routine `cd x && python harness.py capture` or
544	    # `cat foo | python harness.py capture` must not slip past because the first word is benign,
545	    # and a read in one segment must not excuse derivation in another.
546	    for segment in _segments(command):
547	        if _segment_drives_engine(segment):
548	            _refuse("this command drives the work engine (item capture / dispatch / lifecycle)")
549	        if _segment_touches_the_marker(segment):
550	            _refuse("this command removes or rewrites the handover marker this guard runs on")
551	
552	
553	def main():
554	    try:
555	        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
556	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a guard that cannot read its payload must not block a session
557	        _allow()
558	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
559	        _allow()
560	    if str(data.get("hook_event_name") or "PreToolUse") != "PreToolUse":
561	        _allow()
562	    cwd = _cwd(data)
563	    if not _marker_present(cwd):
564	        _allow()  # no handover in progress: invisible no-op
565	    tool = data.get("tool_name")
566	    tool_input = data.get("tool_input") or {}
567	    if not isinstance(tool_input, dict):
568	        _allow()
569	    if tool in FILE_TOOLS:
570	        _handle_file_write(tool_input, cwd)
571	    elif tool in SPAWN_TOOLS:
572	        _refuse("spawning a specialist derives work — that is the restarted PM's act")
573	    elif tool in SHELL_TOOLS:
574	        _handle_shell(tool_input)
575	    elif tool in ASK_TOOLS:
576	        _handle_ask(tool_input)
577	    _allow()
578	
579	
580	if __name__ == "__main__":
581	    main()
